is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l., An. paludis, and An. funestus (page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for the Vgsc L1014F (kdr-west) mutation in An. gambiae s.l. (page 5, 7, 12).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Page 12 states: 'A total of 709 An. gambiae s.l. specimens were successfully analyzed... Of these, 662 were homozygous resistant, 16 were heterozygous, and 31 were homozygous susceptible'.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Kinshasa Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo (page 1, 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a prospective observational cohort study (2018–2022) (page 1, 2).

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is provided for specific health areas and sites: Bu, Kimpoko, and La Voix du Peuple (page 3, 7).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study covers 2018–2022, but the genotype data is presented as an aggregate total (page 12). However, the collection rounds are specified (page 4, S1 Table).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper describes a new longitudinal study (2018-2022) and cites previous work (e.g., Kashamuka et al. 2024) as part of the same cohort study, but this paper presents its own specific entomological data.

supplement.evidence: The required genotype counts are provided in the main text (page 12).

assessment.summary: This longitudinal study (2018-2022) in Kinshasa, DRC, characterized Anopheles species composition, biting behavior, and insecticide resistance. It found An. gambiae s.l. to be the predominant vector, with high resistance to pyrethroids and near-fixation of the L1014F kdr mutation. WHO tube tests showed resistance to DDT and pyrethroids, but susceptibility to bendiocarb and pirimiphos-methyl.
